item.title: Comprehensive ChordPro feature-coverage test song
item.justification: The current test corpus covers features across many focused fixtures, but there is no single test song that exercises all supported language directives and delegate features for a holistic visual completeness review. A consolidated .cho file enables quick inspection across backends and helps confirm that feature interactions render correctly.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: A single .cho test song exists that covers all documented language directives and constructs, with explicit section labels for traceability.
All delegate features (ABC, LilyPond, SVG, Grille, Strum, TextBlock, Program) are exercised with clear, minimal examples and safe defaults.
The test song lives in testing/ with guidance for promotion to t/ after review, per AI-generated test policy.
A visual verification guide exists that lists expected backend outputs and any optional dependencies.

item.title: Refactor HTML5 chord-diagram panel sizing and float behavior for right/top placement
item.justification:
Current HTML5 chord-diagram panel rendering still has coupled layout behaviors across right and top placements: in vertical mode the panel can occupy full available width instead of single-diagram width, and top placement does not consistently let body content flow around the diagram box.
This refactoring isolates panel sizing and placement semantics so layout intent is explicit and behavior-preserving for existing modes: - right + vertical: panel width tracks one chord diagram and remains right-aligned - top: panel participates as a float-like box so song content wraps around it where supported
Related historical fixes (items 38 and 46) addressed stacking direction and wrapper scope; this item focuses on structural CSS/template cleanup to make these rules deterministic and maintainable.

tasks.task: Audit current right/top diagram placement structure in standard and paged song templates and identify where width/stretch behavior is inherited from container rules instead of panel-local rules.

Refactor chord-diagram panel CSS to separate panel sizing from content flow: enforce fit-content/max-content behavior for vertical right placement and explicit right alignment without relying on parent-wide grid stretching.

Refactor top-placement layout so the diagram panel uses float-compatible semantics (or equivalent deterministic flow rule) that allows adjacent song content wrapping while preserving readability and avoiding overlap.
Mirror structural/template changes across standard and paged HTML5 templates to prevent mode drift.
Add/extend regression tests for right+vertical single-diagram-width behavior, right alignment, and top placement content-flow wrapping expectations.
Run focused HTML5 diagram regression suite and confirm no behavior regressions in existing diagram placement cases.

technical-parameters.constraint: Behavior-preserving refactor: no directive/config surface changes and no alteration of diagram SVG payload generation.
Keep compatibility with existing `html5.diagrams.show` and `html5.diagrams.direction` values.
Apply the same structural rules to standard and paged templates.
technical-parameters.pattern: Extract and isolate panel-layout responsibilities from parent wrappers.
Use deterministic width constraints (`fit-content`/equivalent) for vertical right panel sizing.
Prefer CSS-flow semantics over ad-hoc spacing hacks for top placement wrapping.

lessons.lesson: Fixes touching diagram layout must be mirrored across standard+paged templates.
Screen and print outputs should remain visually aligned.
Right-panel stability improves when layout scope is isolated to dedicated wrappers.

test.assertions: With top placement, song body content wraps/flows around the panel per template/CSS contract, with no overlap and stable reading order.

test.assertions: No regressions in previously fixed diagram positioning/containment scenarios.

r.observations: Right-placement stability is improved by forcing the panel to be content-sized at the diagram-container layer (`.cp-chord-diagrams`), not only at the outer wrapper. Top placement now uses a dedicated wrapper with float-based panel flow so body content can wrap beside the diagram box while preserving DOM reading order. Template parity was maintained: both standard and paged song templates now share the same top-wrapper and top-layout class behavior.
r.lessons-learned: Panel sizing constraints must be applied on the element that owns background/border (`.cp-chord-diagrams`), otherwise wrapper-level fit-content rules can still yield full-width visual boxes. When adding a flow-specific layout (top wrap), introducing a dedicated structural wrapper keeps right/top variants isolated and easier to reason about.

item.title: HTML5 print mode emits "page 1" even without TOC

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use config `testing/myconfig_html5.json` with `html5.mode : "print"` and run: `perl script/chordpro.pl testing/lowlands.cho --generate=HTML5 --config=testing/myconfig_html5.json --output=testing/lowlands-debug.html`.
Open `testing/lowlands-debug.html` and inspect generated CSS @page rules.
Observe `@bottom-right { content: counter(page); }` and visible page-number output (e.g. page 1), even when no TOC section is present.

item.expected-result: When TOC is not involved, page-number rendering should be controllable and not appear unexpectedly; users should be able to disable footer page numbers in HTML5 print mode without custom CSS surgery.

analysis.hypothesis: The output is generated in paged mode (`body.chordpro-paged`) because `html5.mode` is set to `print` in the active config. In paged mode, @page margin boxes are always generated from PDF format rules.

`lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5Helper/FormatGenerator.pm` translates `%{page}` to `counter(page)` for footer slots. The effective default PDF format includes a footer page marker, producing `@bottom-right { content: counter(page); }` in generated CSS.

The page number is not TOC-driven in this reproduction. TOC-specific selectors only suppress page numbers on `@page toc`, but no TOC block is required for default page footer counters to appear on song pages.
analysis.root-cause: HTML5 print mode unconditionally inherits PDF format footer semantics for page margin boxes. Because default/effective PDF format contains `%{page}`, the generated CSS includes `counter(page)` and renders page numbers even in no-TOC songbooks.

tasks.task: Add explicit HTML5 print config switch to disable page counters independent of TOC (e.g., `html5.paged.page-numbers: false` or equivalent) and thread it into CSS generation.
Implement conditional suppression in FormatGenerator/layout pipeline so default footer page counters are omitted when the new switch is false.
Verify TOC-specific behavior remains intact (`@page toc` suppression and TOC target-counter rendering unaffected).

Alternative implementation path: document and support a config-only override via `pdf.formats.default.footer` with empty page slot for HTML5 print, without code changes; evaluate if sufficient UX-wise.
Add mirrored regression assertions for generated CSS (`counter(page)` present/absent according to switch or format override) in both HTML5 bugfix suites.

test.description: Generate HTML5 print output with page numbers disabled and verify no default footer `counter(page)` appears for song pages.
test.assertions: No `@bottom-right { content: counter(page); }` rule is emitted when disable switch/override is active.

test.description: Mirror the page-number suppression assertion and ensure TOC page targeting still works when TOC exists.
test.assertions: TOC counters remain functional; only unwanted default page footer counter is suppressed.

test.description: Run `perl script/chordpro.pl testing/lowlands.cho --generate=HTML5 --config=testing/myconfig_html5.json --output=testing/lowlands-debug.html` with the chosen option and inspect output in browser.
test.assertions: "page 1" no longer appears unexpectedly when disabled; behavior is explicit and documented.
